topic: Correct the proposed non-Gaussian PLM minimax-converse topic using the authoritative supplied solution note at ../internal/notes/glm_minimax.tex. Read that file in full. The note refutes the candidate lower-bound conjecture: zeros of the complex MGF yield exact nuisance-annihilating instruments; observable residual transforms F=M H permit contour identification; cumulant separation plus sub-Gaussian compactness gives a finite uniformly conditioned contour bank; and an adaptive split-sample contour estimator is claimed to attain uniform root-n MSE for sufficiently small fixed treatment-nuisance error without an outcome learner. Treat the note’s exact identities and proof sketches as the mathematical seed to audit, complete, correct if needed, and formalize. The research kernel should be the strongest sound Gaussian-versus-non-Gaussian minimax dichotomy or local-to-Gaussian refinement supported by that proof, not the refuted finite-cumulant lower bound. Preserve narrow prior-work framing around classical location-family completeness.

open_problems.open_problem: On one fixed-class independent-noise PLM experiment, is the minimax MSE uniformly of order n^-1 over a cumulant-separated sub-Gaussian non-Gaussian class for sufficiently small fixed treatment-nuisance error and no outcome learner, while the corresponding Gaussian class retains the nuisance-product barrier?

source_refs.claim: The paper proves Gaussian DML minimax optimality and finite-order ACE improvements for independent non-Gaussian treatment noise with a designated nonzero higher cumulant.
source_refs.author: Jikai Jin, Lester Mackey, Vasilis Syrgkanis

source_refs.claim: The paper quantitatively bounds distance to Gaussianity using a zero-free disk of an entire characteristic function.
source_refs.author: Tien-Cuong Dinh, Subhroshekhar Ghosh, Hoang-Son Tran, Manh-Hung Tran

source_refs.excerpt: state a formal dichotomy theorem whose two branches are both on the same experiment as Gu et al.
Add a second open kernel for a uniformly attaining estimator if the product converse fails

open_problems.why_unsolved: The reviewer demanded a dichotomy on one experiment and a uniformly attaining estimator if the product converse fails, while Jin--Mackey--Syrgkanis give a Gaussian lower bound and finite-order non-Gaussian ACE rates rather than an exact-transform root-n theorem. The missing obstacle is uniform spectral strength: pointwise non-Gaussianity does not control the radius, multiplicity, or derivative of a usable complex zero, and an estimated treatment residual adds a nuisance transform whose boundary modulus must stay uniformly away from zero. Compactness, a finite contour bank, pilot measurability, and a uniform empirical-process bound must all hold under the same class quantifiers as the Gaussian converse.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A two-branch minimax theorem on one explicit PLM experiment proving a uniform O(n^-1) MSE contour estimator and matching root-n lower bound on a separated non-Gaussian class, alongside the published Gaussian nuisance-product lower branch, with the spectral separation and fixed-error radius stated quantitatively.

writing_exemplar.why: Its motivation already makes the treatment-noise law the source of the PLM minimax split; the new paper can preserve that arc and replace the finite-order interpretation with exact spectral annihilation.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: black-box nuisance errors limit PLM inference -> Gaussian treatment noise makes DML minimax-optimal -> non-Gaussian noise permits finite-order ACE improvements -> full transform geometry may instead deliver a same-experiment uniform root-n dichotomy

method_exemplars.technique: Use entire-function growth and quantitative Marcinkiewicz stability to turn separation from Gaussianity into a controlled transform-zero region, then combine compact-open continuity with Rouche stability.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The finite contour bank needs precisely the contrapositive bridge from non-Gaussian separation to bounded, stable zero geometry.

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt separate-sample cross-fitting and conditional remainder bounds so residual learning, pilot contour selection, and final contour-moment evaluation are isolated foldwise.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The requested MSE theorem requires uniform control of a learned-nuisance estimating equation after independent data-driven selection.

method_exemplars.technique: Represent complex transform restrictions as stacked real GMM moments and propagate their conditioning through covariance-weighted root-n analysis.
method_exemplars.why_closest: A finite contour bank is a finite collection of complex moments whose boundary conditioning determines the attainable risk.

open_problems.open_problem: What is the sharp local-to-Gaussian minimax risk for the independent-noise PLM when non-Gaussian spectral strength shrinks with n, measured by cumulant separation, nearest-zero radius, or the minimum conditioning of an observable contour bank?

source_refs.claim: The paper establishes qualitatively different Gaussian and non-Gaussian structure-agnostic PLM rates under fixed noise-law conditions but does not give a local-to-Gaussian interpolation.
source_refs.author: Jikai Jin, Lester Mackey, Vasilis Syrgkanis

source_refs.claim: The paper shows that conventional non-Gaussian identification procedures can have size distortions near Gaussian shocks and develops locally robust inference for simultaneous equations.
source_refs.author: Adam Lee, Geert Mesters

source_refs.claim: The paper quantitatively relates the radius of a zero-free characteristic-function disk to closeness to a Gaussian law.
source_refs.author: Tien-Cuong Dinh, Subhroshekhar Ghosh, Hoang-Son Tran, Manh-Hung Tran

source_refs.excerpt: Add Jin--Mackey--Syrgkanis (2025) and state a precise non-overlap
distinguish its binary-treatment and Gaussian-noise frontiers from the bounded continuous-treatment common-code regime.

open_problems.why_unsolved: The PLM literature separates exactly Gaussian laws from fixed non-Gaussian laws, and the prior review asked that their experiments and frontiers be distinguished, but neither supplies a triangular-array experiment in which non-Gaussian information vanishes. Cumulant size, probability distance to Gaussianity, zero-free radius, zero multiplicity, and contour-bank singular value are not interchangeable without new analytic inequalities; as zeros recede, exponential weights inflate variance and nuisance contamination can dominate. Thus no existing result locates the transition among DML, finite-order ACE, and global spectral estimation.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A local asymptotic minimax phase diagram in n, the two nuisance errors, and an explicit spectral-strength sequence, with matching lower bounds and an adaptive estimator in the weak, intermediate, and strongly non-Gaussian regimes.

writing_exemplar.why: Its fixed Gaussian-versus-non-Gaussian contrast is the exact motivation arc to refine into a local phase transition.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Gaussian noise makes DML minimax -> fixed non-Gaussian noise enables ACE gains -> the non-Gaussian signal may vanish with n -> determine the critical spectral scaling and optimal procedure in every regime

method_exemplars.technique: Translate an expanding zero-free disk into quantitative Gaussian approximation and invert that relation to compare spectral radius with a distributional local parameter.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The requested phase diagram needs a rigorous bridge between distance to Gaussianity and the location of usable transform zeros.

method_exemplars.technique: Build separate weak, semi-strong, and strong identification asymptotics and confidence procedures that remain valid across regime boundaries.
method_exemplars.why_closest: A shrinking contour-conditioning modulus creates the same multiple-regime limit-experiment problem as drifting identification strength.

method_exemplars.technique: Localize non-Gaussian identifying information around the Gaussian boundary and construct inference robust to weak non-Gaussianity.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It directly treats approach to Gaussian shocks as weak identification, though in simultaneous equations rather than the PLM.

open_problems.open_problem: Can a split-sample selector over observable complex-MGF contours deliver a uniform asymptotic-linear representation and honest studentized root-n confidence interval for the PLM coefficient when the noise law, useful zero, and zero multiplicity are unknown?

source_refs.claim: The paper gives ACE estimators and plug-in inference after selecting a cumulant order with a nonzero identifying cumulant, rather than inference after searching over complex transform contours.
source_refs.author: Jikai Jin, Lester Mackey, Vasilis Syrgkanis

source_refs.claim: The paper estimates and tests real characteristic-function zeros for completeness under additive independent errors, with pointwise asymptotics requiring an isolated smooth zero.
source_refs.author: Yingyao Hu, Ji-Liang Shiu

source_refs.claim: The paper shows that the limit law of the first empirical characteristic-function zero depends on local population-transform behavior near that zero.
source_refs.author: C. R. Heathcote, J. Huesler

source_refs.excerpt: whether valid root-n DML inference can be recovered when both localized radii are nonparametric.
Add a second open kernel for a uniformly attaining estimator if the product converse fails

open_problems.why_unsolved: A root-n MSE bound does not imply honest coverage after contour selection. Classical zero-estimation theory is pointwise, real-axis, and assumes isolated smooth roots of directly observed variables; ACE inference conditions on a finite chosen cumulant order. Here the empirical MGF is built from learned residuals, the selector can jump between contours near multiple or receding zeros, the winding number is discrete, and the estimation-half denominator can cross zero. Uniform inference therefore requires a measurable fallback rule, foldwise influence expansion, stable zero-count selection, variance bounded away from zero, and control of selection mistakes at the coverage scale.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A fully specified split-sample contour estimator with a uniform influence-function expansion, consistently estimable variance, and honest coverage theorem, plus a counterexample or alternative limit law for weakly conditioned or multiple-zero regimes.

writing_exemplar.why: It provides the closest causal setup and already moves from non-Gaussian moment construction to practical confidence intervals.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: non-Gaussian PLM noise permits scores beyond DML -> ACE inference selects a finite identifying cumulant -> full transforms offer unknown data-dependent contour scores -> obtain honest inference after contour and winding-number selection

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt empirical-characteristic-function zero estimation and its local root asymptotics from real isolated roots to complex contours and estimated residuals.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It is the nearest econometric procedure that estimates transform zeros and conducts inference from their observed-data inheritance.

method_exemplars.technique: Stack complex contour moments into real GMM equations, derive the covariance formula, and studentize the resulting ratio estimator.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Conditional on a selected contour, the estimator is a complex-moment procedure whose variance must be made feasible.

method_exemplars.technique: Use fold-conditional cross-fitting expansions to isolate nuisance fitting and score selection from final evaluation and studentization.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The main causal-inference difficulty is first-order leakage from learned nuisances and data-dependent score choice.

open_problems.open_problem: What necessary and sufficient conditions on treatment-noise independence, transform analyticity, and the residual-learning error D ensure that zeros of the observable transform F=M H certify noise zeros and yield contour identification of the PLM coefficient, and when can zeros of H or dependence destroy that identification?

source_refs.claim: The paper proves that a second-order orthogonal PLM moment exists if and only if the treatment residual is non-Gaussian, using Stein's lemma.
source_refs.author: Lester Mackey, Vasilis Syrgkanis, Ilias Zadik

source_refs.claim: The paper gives location-family completeness conditions using regularity and zero-freeness of the generating characteristic transform.
source_refs.author: Lutz Mattner

source_refs.claim: Under additive independent errors, the paper uses inheritance of an error characteristic-function zero by an observed marginal transform to test completeness.
source_refs.author: Yingyao Hu, Ji-Liang Shiu

source_refs.claim: The paper turns additive separability, independence, and support conditions into completeness-based econometric identification results.
source_refs.author: Xavier D'Haultfoeuille

open_problems.why_unsolved: Classical location-family completeness treats a specified translation operator and function class, while the observable PLM residual transform factors as a noise transform times a learner-error transform only under independence. If H has zeros in the selected region, an observed zero need not be attributable to the noise and the analytic nuisance term can acquire poles; if treatment noise depends on covariates, the scalar factorization itself fails. Existing completeness and higher-order-orthogonality results do not characterize the maximal error class for which H is zero-free or give same-observational-law counterexamples at its boundary.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: An if-and-only-if identification theorem giving an explicit contour functional when F=M H has certifiable noise-zero winding and H is zero-free, paired with observationally equivalent counterexamples or a sharp error-radius failure theorem when those conditions break.

writing_exemplar.why: Its setup already explains how transform zeros of an unobserved additive error can be inherited by an observed marginal; the PLM paper can pivot exactly at the new nuisance-contamination ambiguity.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: location-family completeness is encoded by transform zero-freeness -> additive independence lets observed transforms reveal error zeros -> learned PLM residuals introduce the extra factor H -> characterize when observable winding still identifies the causal coefficient

method_exemplars.technique: Use convolution and Fourier-transform kernel arguments to connect location-family completeness with transform zero geometry for a stated function class.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The contour score is a concrete null vector of the same location-convolution operator whose kernel the identification theorem must characterize.

method_exemplars.technique: Translate primitive independence, additivity, and support assumptions into completeness and then into an econometric identification statement.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It is the closest template for turning an analytic completeness boundary into independently checkable model assumptions.

method_exemplars.technique: Estimate parameters from complex characteristic-function restrictions through spectral GMM and derive feasible asymptotic covariance.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Once the contour functional is identified, this is the nearest established route to an estimator and limit law.

literature_map:
Robinson (1988, Econometrica) is the classical PLM anchor: residualization gives root-n estimation but ordinarily learns both treatment and outcome regressions.
Chernozhukov et al. (2018, Econometrics Journal, arXiv:1608.00060) formalize orthogonal scores and cross-fitting for root-n causal inference with ML nuisances.
Mackey, Syrgkanis, and Zadik (2018, ICML, arXiv:1711.00342) show that second-order PLM orthogonality exists iff treatment residual noise is non-Gaussian.
Balakrishnan, Kennedy, and Wasserman (2023, arXiv:2305.04116) develop structure-agnostic minimax lower bounds for black-box nuisance learning.
Jin and Syrgkanis (2025, COLT, arXiv:2402.14264) establish structure-agnostic optimality for doubly robust ATE/ATT learning.
Jin, Mackey, and Syrgkanis (2025, NeurIPS, arXiv:2507.02275) prove the Gaussian PLM barrier and non-Gaussian ACE improvements from a chosen nonzero higher cumulant.
Jin and Syrgkanis (2025/26, arXiv:2512.17341) give broad sharp DML lower bounds, sharpening the need to isolate the spectral structure that escapes generic models.
Mattner (1992, PTRF) and Isenbeck--Rueschendorf (1992, Probability and Mathematical Statistics) connect location-family completeness to Wiener closure and transform zero-freeness.
Mattner (1993, Annals of Statistics) shows bounded and full completeness can diverge, so the annihilator function class matters.
D'Haultfoeuille (2011, Econometric Theory) turns additive-separability and support conditions into completeness-based econometric identification.
Hu and Shiu (2022, Econometric Reviews) estimate and test inherited real characteristic-function zeros, but only pointwise under isolated-zero conditions and without learned residuals.
Dinh, Ghosh, Tran, and Tran (2021, arXiv:2107.08469) quantitatively relate zero-free characteristic-function disks to Gaussian approximation.
Welsh (1986) and Heathcote--Huesler (1990) study empirical characteristic-function zeros; Chacko--Viceira (2003, JoE) supplies complex-moment spectral GMM inference.
Newey and Robins (2018, arXiv:1801.09138) provide fast cross-fit remainder theory for separating pilot nuisance learning from final moment evaluation.
Lee and Mesters (2024, JoE) and Andrews--Cheng (2012, Econometrica) supply local-to-Gaussian and weak/semi-strong/strong identification templates for a shrinking spectral-strength theory.
